candidates.explanation: Login and refresh both build tokens through getTokensData. The access token is probably signed with the wrong secret, expiry or payload. For example, it may use the refresh secret, or omit or rename the `id` or `role` claims, or `sessionId`. Login and refresh only create tokens and refresh verifies the refresh token with its own strategy, so they still work. The access-token JwtStrategy then rejects every fresh token with 401. I couldn't see this function's body, so this is inferred from the symptoms.

This strategy was not in the retrieved snippets. It verifies access tokens on protected routes. If it uses the wrong secretOrKey (e.g. the refresh secret), sets ignoreExpiration incorrectly, or its validate() returns falsy or throws because of a payload check such as a missing `id`, every request gets a 401 even though login and refresh succeed. The line range is a guess.

fix.description: In getTokensData, sign the access token with the same secret (`auth.secret`) and the expiry (`auth.expires`) that JwtStrategy uses to verify it. Use the refresh secret only for the refresh token. Make sure the access-token payload contains the fields JwtStrategy.validate expects (`id`, `role`, `sessionId`). If the strategy is the faulty side, fix its secretOrKey and validate() so they match.
